title: Balance playtest: ability distribution and tuning
description: Play 10+ full games with all abilities active. Tune: (1) which Suit+Rank combos carry which abilities, (2) ability parameters (Extra Draw count, Double Trouble extra attack count), (3) overall fun — do abilities create interesting decisions or just noise? Track: how often each ability is activated vs played normally, which abilities feel overpowered or useless, whether the game still feels like Durak underneath.
acceptance_criteria: Documented findings (in issue notes). Ability distribution finalized. No ability is never-used or always-used. Games feel meaningfully different from plain Durak.

title: Implement Tier 1 abilities: Trump Changer + Extra Draw
description: Two simple state-mutation abilities. Trump Changer: when activated, changes Engine.Trump to the played card's suit. Once per game (set a flag). Extra Draw: when activated during attack, forces the defender to draw 2 cards from the deck before the defense phase begins. Both abilities consume the card (it goes to discard, not to the bout as an attack/defense).
design: Each ability is a static handler method in a new Abilities class, called by the engine when the player chooses 'ability'. Trump Changer fires a new OnTrumpChanged event so the HUD updates. Extra Draw calls the existing DrawTo mechanism but with an incremented target.
acceptance_criteria: Trump Changer changes the trump suit visually and mechanically. Extra Draw forces 2 cards drawn. Both work for human and AI. Engine smoke test still passes.

title: Engine: ability choice micro-phase
description: When a player plays a card that has an ability, the engine must let them choose: play normally or activate the ability. Add a new Phase or callback pattern so the UI can present a modal and the AI can compute. IPlayerController gets a RequestAbilityChoice method or the engine fires an OnAbilityChoice event. The engine waits for the choice before resolving the play. If the player chooses 'normal', the existing TryAttack/TryDefend path runs unchanged. If 'ability', the engine calls the ability handler instead.
design: Keep the engine synchronous for AI (AI returns the choice immediately) and event-driven for humans (UI shows modal, player clicks, callback resolves). Avoid adding a new Phase enum value if possible — use a pending-choice flag on the engine instead, so the GameLoop knows to wait.
acceptance_criteria: Playing an ability card triggers a choice. Choosing 'normal' behaves identically to the current flow. Choosing 'ability' is a no-op stub for now (individual ability handlers come in later tasks).
close_reason: Engine.TryUseAbility stub added (validates player/phase/ability, consumes card to discard, fires OnAbilityUsed). GameManager routes clicks on ability cards through a choice modal ('Play normally' / 'Use [ability]'). HudView has AbilityChoicePanel. SceneBuilder builds the panel. Smoke test passes. Scene rebuilt.

title: Foundation: AbilityType enum, Card extension, deck composition
description: Add AbilityType enum (TrumpChanger, DoubleDefense, ExtraDraw, Blocker, DoubleTrouble, SeizeInitiative). Extend Card struct with optional AbilityType? field. Create a DeckBuilder that assigns abilities to ~8-10 of 36 cards (configurable mapping). Card equality/hashing must still be based on Suit+Rank only — ability is metadata, not identity.
design: Card stays a value type. AbilityType is nullable so most cards have none. DeckBuilder is a static helper or config ScriptableObject that stamps abilities onto specific Suit+Rank combos. Initial distribution spread across ranks to avoid predictability.
acceptance_criteria: Card has AbilityType? field. DeckBuilder produces a 36-card deck with ~8-10 ability cards. Existing smoke test still passes (abilities are ignored by the greedy AI test policy).
close_reason: AbilityType enum (6 values + display/short/description extensions), Card extended with nullable Ability field (equality still Suit+Rank only), Deck accepts ability config, DeckConfig.DefaultAbilities stamps 10 of 36 cards. Smoke test passes unchanged.

title: Add special card abilities to 2-player prototype
description: Layer 6 special abilities onto the working Durak prototype. Cards with abilities can be played normally (for rank/suit) or activated for their effect — the player chooses. ~8-10 of 36 deck cards carry abilities. Abilities: Trump Changer, Double Defense, Extra Draw (draw 2), The Blocker, Double Trouble (1 extra any-rank attack), Seize Initiative (you become attacker after bout). Deferred to multiplayer: Shield, Reverser. Cut: Magnet, Wildcard.
design: Dual-use cards: every ability card also has a rank+suit. The tension is whether to spend the card for its ability or its combat value. Abilities must deepen Durak's spend/save tension, not bypass it. ~1 in 4 cards carry abilities. Deck composition is configurable so we can tune during playtesting.
acceptance_criteria: All 6 abilities implemented, AI uses them, visual indicator on ability cards, playable in a full game with no frozen states.

title: GameEngine fires Played events before updating Phase, freezing UI
description: Repro: human attacks 8d, AI defends with 9d. HUD stays at 'Knave defends', End bout disabled, no card highlights, even though the bout is fully defended and Phase should now be Attack. Cause: TryAttack and TryDefend invoke their events before assigning Phase, so GameManager.OnDefensePlayed runs UpdateHud+ApplyHighlightForPhase against the still-Defense Phase. After the engine sets Phase=Attack, no event fires to refresh the UI, so the HUD stays stuck. Fix: assign Phase BEFORE firing the event in both TryAttack (Phase=Defense) and TryDefend (Phase=Attack).
close_reason: Fixed: in TryAttack and TryDefend, Phase is now assigned BEFORE the OnAttackPlayed/OnDefensePlayed event fires, so synchronous handlers (UpdateHud, ApplyHighlightForPhase) see the new Phase. Engine smoke test still passes 50/50 games with identical numbers.

title: Smoke test: full playable round, fix obvious bugs
description: Play 5+ complete games as the human, verify rule correctness. Have the AI win and lose. No console errors. No frozen states.
acceptance_criteria: A non-developer could sit down, understand the screen, and finish a game.
notes: Engine-only smoke test PASSED (Wits and Fools/Smoke Test/Play 50 Games): 50 games, 0 stalls, P0=23 / P1=27, avg 13.4 turns. Remaining: human-in-the-loop test — requires Play mode in Unity, click cards, verify rule correctness against the GDD, watch for frozen states or console errors.

title: Build Player abstraction with Hand, plus simple AI policy
description: IPlayer interface + HumanPlayer + AIPlayer. AI policy: defend if possible (lowest valid card), otherwise eat. Attack with lowest non-trump if available. Greedy but legal.
close_reason: IPlayerController + HumanPlayer (no-op, UI drives input) + AIPlayer (greedy: cheapest legal play, prefer non-trump). GameLoop wires controllers to engine via OnTurnBegan event. Smoke test 50/50 games complete with 0 stalls — found and fixed an infinite-loop bug in greedy logic when defender's hand size capped attacks. Engine is correct.

title: Implement game-state machine and rules engine (no UI)
description: States: Setup, Dealing, AwaitingAttack, AwaitingDefense, ResolvingBout, Drawing, GameOver. Pure C# (testable). Implement: trump determination, lowest-trump-goes-first, can-attack, can-defend (higher same suit OR trump), bout resolution (defender eats vs cards discarded), draw-to-min, win condition (last with cards = Fool).
acceptance_criteria: Console smoke test plays a full game between two stub AI players with no UI.
close_reason: GameEngine.cs implements full state machine: Setup/Attack/Defense/Resolving/GameOver. Bout.cs tracks attack/defense pairs. Rules.cs is the single source of truth for Beats/CanAttack/CanDefend. Engine emits events (OnTurnBegan, OnAttackPlayed, OnDefensePlayed, OnBoutResolved, OnDrew, OnGameOver) for UI/AI. Trump = bottom card of deck (visible). Lowest-trump-goes-first. Draw order attacker-then-defender. Win = empty hand when deck empty; Fool = last with cards. Editor menu Wits and Fools/Smoke Test/* runs greedy-AI vs greedy-AI without UI. Compile clean (0 errors).

title: Define core data model: Card, Suit, Rank, Deck, CardData ScriptableObject
description: 36-card deck (6-A, 4 suits). Pure data classes + a CardData SO for any per-card art/metadata override. No MonoBehaviours yet — runtime-only model first.
close_reason: Implemented as pure C# (no MonoBehaviour): Suit enum + glyphs, Rank enum (6-A) + labels, Card readonly struct with equality, Deck with seeded shuffle (36 cards, trump at bottom), Hand. Skipped CardData ScriptableObject — not needed for MVP since cards are just (Suit,Rank) pairs and visuals derive from sprite lookup. SO can be added later if abilities need per-card data.

notes: Per audit: every script fights every other script. Clean slate.

title: Rebuild Wits and Fools prototype from scratch
description: Old prototype is unsalvageable per audit (36+ fixer scripts patching incomplete core systems, claimed phases didn't actually work). Rebuilding clean: 2-player vs AI, core Durak rules, NO special abilities, polished programmer-art visuals.
acceptance_criteria: Playable from start to finish: deal hands, attack, defend, eat-or-discard, draw to refill, win condition. Smooth animations, readable UI, 2-player vs AI.

title: AI ability evaluation policy
description: Extend AIPlayer to decide when to activate abilities vs play cards normally. Heuristics per ability: Trump Changer — activate when holding 3+ cards of the new suit and few of the current trump. Extra Draw — activate when defender has a small hand and deck is large (maximize long-term damage). Blocker — activate when the bout has 2+ attacks and defender wants to stop pile-on. Seize Initiative — activate when losing initiative would be costly (e.g., opponent has few cards). Double Trouble — activate when holding a card that doesn't match bout ranks (the free attack). Double Defense — activate when facing 2+ undefended attacks and the card can cover both.
design: Add an EvaluateAbilityUse method to AIPlayer that returns bool (use ability or play normally). Called by the ability choice callback. Start with simple heuristics; can be tuned during balance testing.
acceptance_criteria: AI uses abilities in reasonable situations. AI does not waste abilities when playing normally would be better. No frozen states when AI has ability cards.

title: CardView ability indicator + ability choice UI + tooltips
description: Visual layer for abilities. (1) Cards with abilities show a small badge/icon and the ability name on the card face. (2) When the human plays an ability card, a modal appears with two buttons: 'Play normally' and 'Use [Ability Name]' plus a one-line description. (3) Hovering over an ability card shows a tooltip with the ability description. AI skips the modal — its policy returns the choice instantly.
design: Ability badge: small colored bar at the bottom of the card face with abbreviated ability name. Modal: a simple Canvas overlay centered on screen, similar to the GameOver panel. Tooltip: a floating TMP_Text that follows the cursor.
acceptance_criteria: Ability cards are visually distinguishable at a glance. The choice modal appears, blocks gameplay until resolved, and routes the choice back to the engine. Tooltips show on hover.

title: Implement Tier 2 abilities: Blocker, Seize Initiative, Double Trouble, Double Defense
description: Four abilities that modify bout rules. The Blocker (defense): sets a flag on the bout preventing the attacker from adding more cards this bout. Seize Initiative (either phase): sets a flag so the activating player becomes attacker after bout resolves, regardless of defense outcome. Double Trouble (attack): grants one additional attack this bout that ignores the rank-match constraint. Double Defense (defense): the played card covers the current undefended slot AND the next one, if both attacks can be beaten by this card's rank or suit.
design: Bout gets new flags: AttacksCapped (for Blocker), and a slot for 'double defense covers two'. GameEngine.ResolveBout checks a SeizeInitiative override for attacker selection. Double Trouble temporarily relaxes CanAttackWith for one play. These are the most complex abilities — each modifies a different part of the rules pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: All four abilities function correctly for human and AI. Edge cases tested: Blocker when attacker has no follow-ups (no-op), Double Defense when only one attack exists (covers just one), Seize Initiative when activator already would have been attacker (no-op), Double Trouble when no legal follow-up rank exists (the extra attack can be any rank).

title: Scene wiring + GameManager bootstrap
description: Single GameScene. GameManager MonoBehaviour bootstraps the rules engine, wires UI references, runs the game loop. No singletons-from-Awake — explicit init order from one entry point.
close_reason: Input task: click-to-play, hover-highlight, end-bout button, and disabled-state visuals all implemented. Scene wiring task: GameScene built by SceneBuilder with explicit GameManager/TableView/HudView wiring; no singletons-from-Awake.

title: HUD/UI: turn indicator, deck count, trump display, win/lose screen
description: Header band shows whose turn + phase ('You attack', 'AI defends'). Show remaining deck count. Trump suit icon + card visible. End-of-game modal: 'You won' or 'You are the Fool'. Restart button.
close_reason: HudView wires turn label, deck count, trump, end-bout button, game-over panel + restart. GameManager keeps all four updated on each engine event. Disabled-button alpha bumped from 0.4 to 1.0 (with darker color) for visibility.

title: Card animations: deal, attack, defend, eat, discard, draw
description: Use coroutines or Unity DOTween (add via Package Manager if not present). Each game action has a visible motion. Keep durations short (~0.25s) so play feels snappy.
close_reason: Implemented as part of GameManager: dealing visuals (instant on setup), attack/defense/eat moves use coroutine-based ease-out-cubic to bout slots, eat absorbs visuals back into hand, discard moves cards to discard slot then destroys them. No DOTween dependency needed. ~0.22s per move per design (snappy).

title: Input + interaction: click/drag-to-play, valid-target highlighting
description: On player turn: hover highlights valid plays. Click a card to attack OR defend the leftmost undefended attacker. Disabled-state visuals for invalid plays. End-bout button when human is attacker and decides not to add more.
notes: Added disabled-state visuals: invalid plays during the human's turn render with CanvasGroup.alpha=0.45 and a faint gray outline (was previously identical to off-turn = no outline). OnClicked is now nulled on disabled/off-turn cards so disabled clicks no-op cleanly. Engine smoke test (50 games) passes: 23/27 split, 0 stalls, avg 13.4 turns/game.
close_reason: Input task: click-to-play, hover-highlight, end-bout button, and disabled-state visuals all implemented. Scene wiring task: GameScene built by SceneBuilder with explicit GameManager/TableView/HudView wiring; no singletons-from-Awake.

title: Table layout: hand fan, opponent hand (face-down), deck, trump, discard, attack/defense slots
description: Top-down 'table' layout per GDD. Player hand bottom (fan), opponent hand top (face-down stack). Center: deck stack with trump card sticking out from under it, discard pile, and bout slots (attacks top row, defenses overlapping below). Use Canvas + Layout Groups with manual positioning where the auto-layout fights us.
close_reason: Built TableView, HandLayout, HudView. SceneBuilder editor menu reproducibly builds the entire scene: Camera, EventSystem, Canvas with felt+frame, HUD bar, deck stack, trump slot, discard slot, bout area, two HandLayouts, end-bout button, game-over panel, GameManager. Game runs in play mode (verified via screenshot). Issue found: TMP Essential Resources never imported in this project — fixed in PrefabBuilder/SceneBuilder by detecting missing font and importing automatically.

title: Card prefab + visual rendering (face up/down, suit, rank)

PrefabBuilder editor menu builds CardView.prefab procedurally — repeatable, no manual hand-tweaking. 110x160px, programmer-art with TMP text, red/black suit colors, dark-red back with W&F label.

title: Verify beads is working

value: Wits&Fools engine smoke test: menu 'Wits and Fools/Smoke Test/Play 50 Games (Greedy AIs)' or via Unity_ManageMenuItem. Runs 50 deterministic games with greedy AIs vs each other. Healthy result: 0 stalls (safety cap), roughly balanced wins, avg ~13 turns/game. Prints to Unity console — read with FilterText='Smoke Test'.

unity-mcp bridge (com.unity.ai.assistant relay) drops when Unity does a domain reload (Play mode entry while compiling, or RunCommand crashes inside Unity). Doesn't auto-recover; requires /mcp reload in Claude Code. Workaround: wait for compile to fully finish before pressing Play. Time penalty per drop: ~30 seconds + user interaction.

Wits&Fools: GameLoop initially Pumped() synchronously inside OnAttackPlayed handler, which caused AI to act before GameManager's visual handler ran (subscriber order). Refactored to GameLoop.Tick() called per-frame from GameManager.Update; AI ticks delayed by AiThinkSeconds for deliberate pacing. Avoids re-entering engine inside its own events.
